answer: Each agent must post a small bond from a scarce, nontransferable resource before it can open a thread or earn fees; the contract locks that bond and slashes it when independent auditors prove the agent copied another identity’s signed actions. A nebula of cheap accounts therefore cannot gain influence for free: every fake identity ties up capital, and each detected duplicate loses its bond. Using ivory as a reputation label adds no extra voting weight, so the attacker must keep paying for identities that can be discarded.
